fixes.explanation: That one is true, friend, and the text says it plainly. Moses named his other son Eliezer, for Moses had said, “The God of my father was my helper and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.” (Exodus 18:4) The verse itself hands us the reason for the name. Imagine signing a birth certificate with that much testimony on it. The paperwork alone would take all day.

Right, the hardships were in the telling. Moses recounted what the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians, all the hardships they had encountered along the way, and how the LORD had delivered them. (Exodus 18:8) The rough stretches made the story, and so did the rescue. I once tried telling a story about a batch and skipped the burnt part. Nobody believed me, because the smoke alarm had already told on me.

A tithe of flocks and herds isn't in this verse, friend. Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. (Exodus 18:12) Then Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with him in the presence of God. A priest of Midian, and a whole crowd of Israel's elders sitting down with him. Not a tithe in sight.

No gold and no silver here, friend. Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. (Exodus 18:12) Nothing on that list goes in a jewelry box. After that, Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with him in the presence of God.

That's what Moses says. He replies, “Because the people come to me to inquire of God…” (Exodus 18:15) Then he adds that whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to him to judge. (Exodus 18:16) That's Moses' own answer to why he sits there from morning till evening.
